section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Linear Transformation
section_1.content: Briefly introduce vectors and how a 2x2 matrix transforms the 2D plane. Visual focus: A unit square (defined by vectors i and j) being stretched or sheared into a parallelogram.
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic arm moving from point (1,0) to (2,1); the matrix captures how the underlying grid deforms.

section_2.title: Defining the Determinant
section_2.content: Define the determinant as the 'area scaling factor' of the transformation. If the transformation maps a shape to a region, the determinant is how many times the original area has expanded or shrunk.
section_2.example: If a 1x1 square transforms into a parallelogram with an area of 5, the determinant of the transformation matrix is 5.

section_3.title: The Meaning of Sign and Zero
section_3.content: Explain that a negative determinant means the transformation involves a 'flip' (reflection). A zero determinant means the transformation squashes the plane into a line or point, losing a dimension.
section_3.example: Think of a 'magic mirror'—a positive determinant is a clear image, a negative one is a reflection, and a zero determinant is like squashing a 3D cat into a 2D flat paper cutout.

section_4.title: Calculation Method (The 2x2 Case)
section_4.content: Introduce the standard formula det([[a, b], [c, d]]) = ad - bc. Connect the formula back to the visual geometry of the parallelogram side lengths.
section_4.example: Calculate the determinant of matrix [[3, 1], [0, 2]]. Show the visual result: the unit square becomes a rectangle with base 3 and height 2, area = 6.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Application
section_5.content: Summarize that the determinant is a core diagnostic tool for matrices—telling us if a system has a unique solution (non-zero) or is singular (zero).
section_5.example: In computer graphics, if your determinant is 0, your 3D model has collapsed into a flat shape—your code has a bug!

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
